notes: USD 5.50 a year is USD 0.458 a month on annual prepay, and USD 5.50 is the money out of pocket. The store page lists eighteen annual prices between USD 4.99 and USD 60.00 without a machine-readable plan pairing in the extracted text, so which tier carries the USD 4.99 minimum is not established; the USD 5.50 headline is the vendor's own statement and is what this record prices. TUN/TAP is stated as enabled, which is the LXC feature WireGuard actually needs; that it is enabled on the USD 4.99 plan specifically was not checked. A 2026-10-24 re-read found the NL 256MB NAT rung at USD 4.99 a year, below the USD 5.50 LXC rung this record originally priced, with the same 20 NAT ports, UDP and TCP, TUN/TAP, one IPv6 and 800 GB. The store group is /store/ovz-nat-vps and natvps.html calls the same products OpenVZ while the store heading says LXC, so the guest shares the host kernel either way. The store says 'Risk-free for 2 days' while the marketing pages and FAQ say 3 days; the store figure is quoted here. Crypto is excluded from the refund. Two plans, SA 256MB and SG 400MB, read 'NO' for IPv6, so one IPv6 per plan is not a site-wide fact. ⛔ THE COUNTERPARTY IS DISSOLVED. Companies House returns 'Dissolved on 26 December 2023' for KHAN WEB HOST LTD, company number 13550380, incorporated 2021-08-05, and natkvm.net still prints 'Registered in England & Wales (Company No: 13550380)' while naming no successor entity. Two public refund refusals on annual plans sit on either side of that date: a LowEndTalk thread of December 2024 reports a VPS offline repeatedly within a week and an IPv6 changed without notice, refund refused because the order was 'older than 3 days'; a January 2026 thread reports NAT rules not applied on delivery and a refund denied inside the advertised 48-hour window because it was paid in crypto. A third reports 'almost every day I get network outages that can last for hours'. Against that, one 2024 review of a Turkey node was positive. The money at risk is USD 4.99, so this is a small-stakes decision, but a reader should treat it as a write-off bet rather than a purchase with recourse. | 2026-10-24: this is the only seller in the market that states UDP in writing on a dedicated page, and it is also the one with first-hand reports that UDP is filtered until a ticket is opened. The marketing sentence and the June 2024 thread cannot both be the whole truth; what they are consistent with is a default-deny rule that support can lift per customer, which is a different product from 'UDP out-of-the-box'. Combined with a dissolved counterparty, this row is a write-off bet rather than a WireGuard node for a year. Verdict moved from 'qualifies' to 'qualifies-with-caveat' on that evidence. Provenance of the rows in this record: the LowEndSpirit thread and the UDP finding were read
